The Gatha forms dars'ishyasi for drakshyast, sunishyati for s'roshyati, hshipishyats for kshepsyati, and spris'ishyatt for sparkshyati or sprakshyati, are analogous to the Pali forms vedissdmi for vetsydmi, bhunjissdmi for bhokshymt, and dessissami for dekshydmi. The G&tha past indeclinable particles also, such as bhavitud, ramitud, hanitvd, labhitvd, stuvitvd manitvd, vijihitvd, s'unitod, spris'iivd for 074८६४८, mantva, hatvi, labdh vd, stutvd, matvd, vithitvd, s'rutvd, and sprishtvd, are formed on the same principle as the similar Pali ones, pavisitud, = 747४८०८, bhunjitvd, for pra+vesh{vd, jndtvd,; and bhukivd. Of the forms karitya and kariydna for kritvi, the latter coincides in its termination with such Lali forms as sutvdna and disvdna for grutvd and drishjvd. Again, we have the forms kampayantéd, vdrdyanto, vinishkramanto, viryavanto (part. nom, sing.), for kampayan, etc., which coincides with the Pali and Prakrit. The same may be said of pekshasi for prekshase + tdéva for tévat; smardhi, kurvahi, bhanéhi, vasdhi, for smara, kuru, bhana and vasa respectively ; deviye and deviye for devydh ; tapasmi for tapast ; talasmin for tale ; arhantebhih for arhadbhih + prabhaya for prabhiyd, vadchéyd for vdchd. For tyaktvé I find the word chhorayitod, which does not seem to be much used in Sansh rit, though Wilson, in his Dictionary, gives chhorae na in the sense of "leaving."
